plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial with dense, layered flower heads in a huge range of forms, from pompons to spiders. It is one of the last garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere and tolerates light frost. Flowering is triggered by the shortening days of autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; originated in China and widely grown in Japan, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is the name of the Japanese imperial seat. In Chinese culture they are one of the Four Noble Plants.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, semi-deciduous tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When the blooms fall, they carpet streets and gardens in purple. In the Southern Hemisphere it is at its peak in the spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina and Brazil
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, and the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. In parts of Australia, a flower falling on your head is said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often lightly fragrant flowers. Unlike the related Camellia japonica, it blooms in autumn and early winter, brightening gardens when little else is in flower. It is a valuable late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to produce a cooking and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub bearing the largest flower head of any protea, a bowl-shaped crown of stiff pink bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It grows in the fynbos and is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and periodic fires. The flowers are long-lasting and popular as cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer (September to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape and Eastern Cape of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the family Proteaceae is named after Proteus, the shape-shifting Greek sea god, because of its great diversity of forms.
